answer: Each identity leases one distinct artesian well plot outside any oasis zone and registers its pump meter with the county. Monthly, inspectors read the meter, check a cipher seal on the pump head, and post the flow hash; a dry or shared well loses standing. Output must stay above a set nadir of 4,000 litres monthly, proving real upkeep. 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 drilled wells at $3,800 each ($3.8 million), $60 monthly inspection each, and real maintenance; trade-off: arid districts have few drillable plots, so admission is geographically uneven.
